text:
infra-monitor: INCIDENT detected — sudden p99 latency spike on streaming endpoint `/v1/stream` (us-west-2). p95 baseline ~280ms -> 1.2s, p99 ~3.4s. error rate stable but a bunch of streaming stalls observed. alert id: INC-1864509123 :rotating_light:

deploy-bot: Deployment `prefix-hash-v2` rolled at 1864503000 to infra cluster gw-prod-3. No automatic rollbacks triggered.

eva: I'm oncall. Pulling traces and slow logs now. First glance: increased KV cache miss rate on prefix cache for streaming keys. miss_rate ~ 58% (normal ~8%).

mike: Confirming metrics — paging to disk increased on stream-workers. per-shard paging ops up 4x, eviction rate spiked. Looks correlated with commit `git://infra/prefix-hash@a7b2f3c` that changed prefix length from 8 -> 10.

raj: screenshot of dashboard: `streaming.kv.cache.hit_rate` shows drop to 42% at 18:02 UTC, `streaming.p95` jump at same time. Also seeing a ~30% increase in tail IO latency on the NVMe nodes.

amy: The prefix-hash change altered bucket distribution; some hot prefixes now map to many more shards causing cache sharding imbalance. That explains evictions and miss amplification.

eva: Customers impacted? quick check on customer-facing errors: none to 5xx, but partial streaming responses and stalls for long responses. Triage note: SLOs breached for p95 and p99 streaming latency. Potential customer impact: interactive agents and streaming UIs may stall or show delayed partials.

mike: Mitigation options: 1) rollback prefix-hash commit (fast but requires deploy), 2) force cache warmup by synthetic fanout to hot prefixes, 3) increase in-memory cache per-shard temporarily, 4) fallback to old prefix length in routing layer.

raj: I can push a rollback to the canary (gw-canary) in ~6 minutes. That would let us validate reduced miss-rate before doing prod.

eva: Do the canary first. Meanwhile enable streaming fallback: if KV cache miss count > 5 within 2s, route to cold-path that uses larger batch windows to avoid per-token stalls. amy, can runtime flip that flag dynamically?

amy: Yes, runtime has `streaming.fallback_on_kvmiss` flag. I can enable it cluster-wide with a small runtime config push. It will add ~80ms to median but should stop streaming stalls. Pushing change in 2m.

deploy-bot: Deploy started: rollback plan `prefix-hash-rollback-canary` -> gw-canary. rollout id: r-1864509200.

raj: Canary rollback applied to gw-canary. Monitoring hit/miss in canary: hit_rate recovering from 46% -> 86% over 3m.

mike: Nice. p95 on canary dropped from 980ms -> 310ms, p99 from 3.2s -> 450ms.

eva: Amy — please enable fallback flag now. Also, create a temporary alert suppression for non-actionable paged IO alerts so we don't noise the channel.

amy: Enabling `streaming.fallback_on_kvmiss=true` across us-west-2 now. Suppression rule added for alert group paging-io-spike for 30m.

infra-monitor: Canary metrics: `streaming.kv.cache.hit_rate` 85% on canary, global prod still 44%. Rollback to prod queued pending verification window (10m).

eva: Running synthetic warmup traffic for top 50 prefixes to pre-warm caches in prod. Script: 
```
for p in $(cat top-prefixes.txt); do curl -s "https://gw-prod-*/v1/stream?prefix=$p&warm=1" &
done
```
Synthetic load started at 18:25 UTC.

mike: After warmup + fallback, global p95 improved to ~340ms, p99 to ~520ms, miss_rate fell to 28% (still above baseline). Planning full rollback.

raj: Rolling back `prefix-hash-v2` to prod now. Rollback id r-1864509400. Estimated completion 3m.

deploy-bot: Rollback to `prefix-hash-v1` completed on prod at 18:33 UTC (1864509580).

amy: Monitor shows hit_rate back to 91% within 3m. paging ops and NVMe tail latency returning to baseline. Streaming stalls subsided.

eva: Customer impact summary for the incident window (18:01-18:35 UTC): SLO breach on p95/p99 for streaming for ~34 minutes. No increase in 5xxs, but several customers reported user-visible stalls in streaming sessions (internal estimate ~12 customers, high-usage chatbots most affected). Post-incident follow-ups: revert prefix-hash change from feature branch until we can analyze distribution and add pre-deploy load-tests.

mike: Action items assigned: 
- amy: add canary-level distribution check and unit test for prefix distribution (due EOD).
- raj: add safe-rollback job to deploy pipeline to make canary->prod rollback automated (24h).
- eva: create incident writeup + customer notification draft (in progress).
- infra: run offline analysis to compute expected bucket imbalance for prefix lengths 6-12 (48h).

eng_oncall: Handoff: eva -> mike at 19:00 UTC. I will take over postmortem coordination. Next oncall notes: keep fallback flag available for 48h.

eva: Thanks team. I'll start the incident writeup and tag affected customers. Closing channel once postmortem posted. :white_check_mark:
